content: Melvin-Koushki says that, in this historical reading, the lettrists take the insights of theoretical mysticism and philosophy and, returning to the raw text of revelation, synthesize the whole into a new master science predicated on the occult effusions of the Imams and the ancients; the ascent from literalism and return to lettrism constitutes the full ambit of human knowledge, comprising all the Islamic and pre-Islamic sciences rendered into a standardized, efficient, hyperliteral tool for analysing the constituent atoms of the two Books, the Quran and the cosmos.
refers_to_primary: Ibn Turka, R. Shaqq-i Qamar u Bayān-i Sāʿat
